## Catalina Islands in Costa Rica: boat trips and fishing off Guanacaste

**The Catalina Islands are a group of rocky islands off Costa Rica's northwestern Pacific coast.** Boats travel here from the Playa Flamingo area and neighbouring ports in Guanacaste. The seascapes, fishing and underwater life make this a different kind of outing from an ordinary day on a sandy beach.

The islands lie in open waters. Weather, swells and currents determine whether boats can set out. A fishing or diving programme therefore needs to reflect the actual conditions of the day, rather than a guaranteed list of sites.

## What kind of fishing is available around Catalina?

The coastal waters around the islands include rocky areas inhabited by various fish species. Fishing programmes on the northern Pacific coast mention roosterfish, snappers, jacks and other inshore fish. The potential catch, however, changes with the season and conditions.

**Inshore fishing and going offshore into deeper water are different options.** The former takes place closer to the islands and reefs. The latter may involve a longer journey to deeper waters in search of pelagic species. These formats differ in price, duration and the vessel's equipment.

| Question | What to confirm |
|---|---|
| Where you fish | Near the islands or offshore |
| How long it takes | Travel and fishing time |
| What is included | Tackle, food and permits |
| Weather conditions | Whether a safe departure is possible |

Ask the local operator about the crew, lifesaving equipment and procedures for postponing a trip in bad weather. No sea fishing tour can guarantee a particular catch.

## The islands' underwater life

Catalina is also known for diving. Underwater, there are rocky reefs, outcrops, shoals of fish and different ray species. At favourable times, divers may see large manta rays, but encounters with wild animals depend on nature and cannot be guaranteed.

Diving requires an operator, the appropriate certification or training programme, and consideration of depth, currents and visibility. Snorkelling at the surface and scuba diving are distinct activities. If underwater encounters are the goal, choose a specific dive site suited to your experience.

Sea conditions in Guanacaste change from day to day. Even with clear skies ashore, strong winds and waves can affect the islands. For this reason, a boat outing should not be planned as an obligatory activity during a brief connection between flights.

## Organising your trip

Trips usually begin on [Costa Rica's Pacific coast](/costa-rica/place/pacific-coast/), in the Flamingo area and neighbouring resorts. Before booking, confirm the exact departure port, the distance from your hotel to the pier and the expected return time.

If the itinerary combines the islands with a stay in [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/), a separate road transfer will be needed. Even beaches that are geographically close are not always connected by a direct coastal road.

## What to bring

For a boat trip, wear sun-protective clothing, a secured hat and non-slip shoes, and protect your belongings from salty spray. If you get seasick, discuss preventive measures with a doctor or pharmacist beforehand. Drinking water and familiarity with onboard safety rules matter more than extra luggage.

For diving, allow the appropriate interval before your next flight and follow your instructor's recommendations. For fishing, find out the local rules for handling catches and protecting the marine environment.

## What to combine with the Catalina Islands

A day at sea complements a beach holiday when the weather permits. On the coast you can also make time for surfing, walks and other water activities; simply staying near Flamingo does not mean that fishing is included in your hotel arrangements.

We can help coordinate your choice of marine activities with a wider journey around Costa Rica. Compare our [Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/) and [fishing-themed travel collection](/interests/fishing/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Catalina Islands

### Are the Catalina Islands visited only for fishing?

No. Besides fishing trips, the area is known for diving and boat excursions. Your choice depends on experience and weather conditions.

### Are manta ray sightings guaranteed?

No. Manta rays are wild animals, and encounters depend on the season, underwater conditions and animal behaviour.

### Can we depart from Tamarindo?

Guanacaste has several ports and operators. Confirm the exact pier, transfer and departure time for your chosen outing.

## Which Ada Tours itinerary visits the Catalina Islands?

The [Catalina Islands](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/) lie off Costa Rica's northwestern Pacific coast, near the province of Guanacaste. These rocky islands and their surrounding waters are known to divers and fishing enthusiasts.

We currently offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting Catalina. The available itinerary is the [13-day “Extreme Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/). It combines a range of activities across the country, with the island excursion forming part of the final Pacific-coast section.

**An important distinction:** this is an extensive adventure tour with a full programme of jungles, volcanoes and the ocean coast. It is not presented as a Catalina-only diving package. If the main purpose of your holiday is to spend several days exclusively underwater, do not assume that the ready-made 13-day programme already includes repeated dives.

## What exactly is planned at Catalina?

Marine activities on this itinerary take place on two consecutive days.

| Day | Activity |
|---|---|
| 10 | Sport fishing near Flamingo |
| 11 | Scuba diving at the Catalina Islands |

On day 10, participants go fishing around [Flamingo](/costa-rica/place/flamingo/). The programme describes both deep offshore waters and areas closer to shore near the Catalina Islands. Possible catches include marlin, tuna, mahi-mahi and various inshore fish. This is specifically a fishing day, not a diving day.

Day 11 includes **scuba diving at the Catalina Islands**. It is designed for experienced divers: currents and difficult surface conditions are possible. The programme describes sites at depths of 12 to 35 metres, drift diving at some locations, rays and reef sharks.

The two days at sea are consecutive but have different objectives and requirements. If you are interested only in fishing, explore [fishing tours in Costa Rica](/interests/fishing/tours/costa-rica/). For more underwater itineraries, see the [Costa Rica diving tours collection](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/). Both collections cover other locations as well, whereas this catalogue selects trips specifically featuring Catalina.

## Why the diving here is attractive

The marine environment around Guanacaste is characterised by rocky underwater formations and conditions influenced by currents and the seasonal upwelling of colder water from depth. The professional diving association PADI identifies the Catalina Islands as a well-known diving destination on this coast.

Divers can encounter rays, fish, moray eels and sharks, and, at the right time, large manta rays. Costa Rican tourism materials particularly highlight the possibility of seeing giant oceanic manta rays near Catalina. However, **a particular manta encounter is never guaranteed**: marine animals move freely, while visibility may change during a single day.

The underwater landscape matters too. This is not shallow-water swimming at a beach: features of the local dive sites include rocks, depth changes and drifting along submerged formations. Site selection must take account of each participant's qualifications, the weather and the professional dive operator's judgement.

The [Catalina Islands destination page](/costa-rica/place/catalina-islands/) describes the natural site and its connection with sea fishing. This article focuses on how the visit fits into a real Ada Tours itinerary.

## Manta season and ocean conditions

One reason divers are interested in Catalina is the seasonal chance of encountering large manta rays. Materials from Costa Rica's tourism institute identify January to April as the most characteristic months for such sightings in Guanacaste; local dive operators give a broader window from late December to May.

The dry season on land does not mean that the sea will be equally calm. During this time, Papagayo winds and the upwelling of cooler water affect the country's northwest. These conditions can support abundant marine life while also increasing swell, changing underwater temperatures and reducing visibility.

It helps to distinguish two objectives when choosing dates. If maximising the chance of seeing manta rays matters most, consider the animals' seasonal activity. If calm conditions and a comfortable individual dive are more important, the decision depends on the weather, wind and your experience. No calendar month simultaneously guarantees perfect visibility, calm seas and encounters with large animals.

Whether a boat can depart and which dive sites can be used always depend on current conditions. Assess a programme by its stated activities and safety requirements, rather than promises of seeing a particular species.

## Who is the diving day designed for?

In the [“Extreme Costa Rica” programme](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), the Catalina day is intended for **more experienced divers**. Sites differ in depth and current conditions. Safe descent, buoyancy control and safety-stop skills are practically important.

The maximum depth listed for some sites is not a recommendation for every participant to dive that deep. Permissible depth is determined by qualifications, experience, medical restrictions, briefing and the operator's rules. Beginners may have very different limits, so they should establish in advance whether a suitable alternative is available.

If you are travelling with family or friends and not everyone scuba dives, agree a separate plan for the day at sea. The tour programme does not automatically confirm snorkelling from the same boat, a private instructor for a beginner or another excursion in place of the dive.

Also plan the interval between your last dive and any flight according to the certification organisation's and dive operator's recommendations. This is particularly important when the marine activity falls near the end of your journey.

## How Catalina fits into the 13-day itinerary

[“Extreme Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/) combines very different natural and sporting activities. The route begins in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), the forested areas of [Braulio Carrillo](/costa-rica/place/braulio-carrillo-national-park/) and [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), then takes in the [Pacuare River](/costa-rica/place/pacuare-river/), the [Arenal region](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and the cloud forests of [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/).

Activities on land and water are included, with Guanacaste's coast appearing towards the end. Fishing at Flamingo and diving at Catalina follow the inland natural regions. The journey then continues through [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/) towards its conclusion.

Keep this in mind when choosing: **Catalina is one memorable day, not the main geographical focus of all 13 days**. The tour suits people who want to alternate jungle, adventure, ocean and rest, rather than dedicate every day to one sport.

## Catalina or Caño Island: how do the routes differ?

Both places are on Costa Rica's Pacific coast, but their geographical settings differ. Catalina is associated with the country's northwest and the Flamingo area, whereas [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/) is near the southwestern Osa Peninsula and Drake Bay.

| Destination | Main tour context |
|---|---|
| Catalina | Fishing and diving off Guanacaste |
| [Caño](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/tour/) | Corcovado, snorkelling and scuba diving |

The ready-made trips differ as well. The Catalina itinerary described here has a diving day for experienced participants. [Routes through Caño](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/tour/) include both snorkelling and scuba-diving options, including short five-day trips.

If a particular marine activity is important, choose based on the day-by-day description, rather than the generic words “island” or “Pacific Ocean”. Travelling between the two destinations takes time; Ada Tours' existing programmes do not present them as neighbouring stops on a single day.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many current Ada Tours trips visit Catalina?

The current number is shown in this collection and updates with the catalogue. In the verified selection, the principal published option is the [13-day “Extreme Costa Rica” tour](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/).

### Which day is the diving scheduled for?

On the 13-day itinerary, diving at the Catalina Islands is scheduled for **day 11**. Day 10 is reserved for sport fishing near Flamingo.

### Can giant manta rays be seen at Catalina?

There is a possibility, especially during their season of activity. Encounters with wild animals cannot be guaranteed, however, and the quality of a dive depends on current ocean conditions.

### Is diving at Catalina suitable for beginners?

The published Ada Tours programme specifically describes a day for more experienced divers, with possible currents and deep sections. Beginners need to agree a suitable alternative format in advance, if one is available.

### Does fishing take place on the same day as diving?

No. In [“Extreme Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-extreme-adventure/), these are separate days: fishing on day 10 and diving on day 11.

### Where else can I find trips with underwater activities?

Alongside this itinerary, see [Costa Rica diving-themed tours](/interests/diving/tours/costa-rica/) and [tours via Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/tour/). Compare the specific included activity, experience requirements and geography of the whole trip.

## Corcovado National Park: Osa Peninsula nature and visiting rules

Corcovado is in southwestern Costa Rica on the [Osa Peninsula](/costa-rica/place/osa-peninsula/). Dense lowland rainforest reaches the Pacific Ocean here, and visitor routes wind among trees, streams and coastal habitats. It is a destination for travellers who want to spend time inside a protected natural area and observe wild animals.

**Choose a specific Corcovado sector and make a reservation before travelling.** The park has several entrances, with different arrival arrangements. Simply saying “a Corcovado excursion” does not provide enough information for planning.

## Corcovado's sectors: which should you choose?

The SINAC conservation authority lists six sectors open to visitors: Sirena, San Pedrillo, La Leona, Los Patos, Los Planes and El Tigre. Each has its own approaches, trails and rules.

| Sector | Main feature |
|---|---|
| Sirena | Ranger station and forest trails |
| San Pedrillo | Coastal rainforest |
| La Leona | Hiking routes beside the ocean |
| Los Patos | Longer forest crossings |
| El Tigre | Local forest trail |

### Sirena: walks from the ranger station

Sirena is one of the national park's best-known sectors. Trails around the station pass through humid rainforest. Walks focus on birds, mammals and vegetation; proceeding slowly and listening to the forest is often more rewarding than trying to cover the greatest possible distance.

A day visit and an overnight hike need different arrangements. Accommodation and meals at the station are booked separately, so do not assume space will be available without confirmation.

### San Pedrillo, La Leona and forest crossings

San Pedrillo combines coastal routes with forest. La Leona lies in another part of the park reached on foot. Los Patos is associated with longer forest treks; these should not be treated as a short stroll from a boat landing.

**A guide is mandatory on the La Leona–Sirena and Los Patos–Sirena routes** under SINAC rules. For other sectors, confirm admission and guiding requirements in advance. Visitors cannot simply move freely between all the entrances without the required arrangements.

## Which animals can you see in Corcovado?

The forests of the Osa Peninsula are home to monkeys, tapirs, peccaries and many birds. Scarlet macaws are among the area's conspicuous bird species. The park also protects habitats of rarer animals. However, **the presence of a species in the forest does not guarantee a sighting during an excursion**.

Rain, time of day, noise and the guide's experience affect wildlife observation. Animals must not be fed, touched or chased for photographs. Binoculars are useful for birdwatching, while a suitable camera lens lets you keep your distance.

Corcovado's environment differs from [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/), whose main attraction is montane cloud forest, and [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), where travellers explore canals and coastal ecosystems. Compare these regions in the [Costa Rica wildlife tours catalogue](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/).

## Getting to Corcovado

### Drake Bay and boat journeys

[Drake Bay](/costa-rica/place/drake-bay/) is one base for travel around the northwestern Osa Peninsula. Boat transfers depart from the coast for certain Corcovado sectors. Swell can affect departure and travel time even when the main activity is a hike.

A route through [Sierpe](/costa-rica/place/sierpe/) may include a boat along the river and mangrove channels to the ocean coast. But **a transfer to Drake Bay and official entry into the park are separate stages**. Confirm the sector, direction of travel and transfer timing for the specific programme.

### Southern approaches and Caño Island

Other entrances are associated with Puerto Jiménez and Carate, where separate hiking routes begin. Do not count on a quick transfer between Corcovado entrances without checking distances and road conditions.

[Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/) lies off the peninsula and is a destination for marine excursions. A visit to the island and a walk in Corcovado are **different visits**, even if they take place during the same journey. Their sea conditions and admission requirements can differ.

## Park reservations and restrictions

Visiting Corcovado requires advance booking under SINAC procedures. Places are limited, and rules vary by sector. It is best to agree your entry date before finalising complex transfers around the Osa Peninsula.

Leaving designated trails, feeding or chasing animals, littering and **swimming off beaches inside the national park because of strong currents** are prohibited. Single-use plastics and bringing food are subject to restrictions; special rules apply in the Sirena sector.

For hiking, bring comfortable closed non-slip shoes, protection against heavy rain, water and waterproof storage for belongings. Check equipment, food and permitted luggage against the rules of your sector and your boat or road-transfer arrangements.

## When to visit and how much time to allow

Corcovado has a hot, very humid climate. The Pacific coast is generally relatively drier from December to April, but rain is possible throughout the year. During wetter months, trail conditions and the sea may have a greater effect on access.

For a day visit, include the whole journey to the sector and back. If the nature of the Osa Peninsula is your principal aim, it is better to allow **several days in the region**, spreading forest walks, marine activities and rest across your stay and leaving some flexibility for weather. This is planning advice, not a fixed tour duration.

Find current itineraries in [tours visiting Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/tour/) and wider options in [Costa Rica tours](/costa-rica/tour/). Compare the sector, guiding arrangements and paid transfers before choosing.

## Frequently asked questions about Corcovado

### Can I enter Corcovado without a reservation?

No. Under SINAC rules, visiting requires an advance reservation for your chosen sector.

### Is a guide mandatory?

A guide is compulsory on the La Leona–Sirena and Los Patos–Sirena routes. Confirm the requirements for other sectors when booking.

### Can I swim at Corcovado's beaches?

Swimming off beaches inside the national park is prohibited because of strong currents. Other authorised stretches of coast are available for seaside activities.

### Are Corcovado and Caño Island the same excursion?

No. They are separate natural areas and different programmes. You can combine them if time, transfers and weather permit.

## Which tours visit Corcovado National Park?

[Corcovado National Park](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/) lies on the Osa Peninsula in southwestern Costa Rica. This protected rainforest borders the Pacific Ocean. Visitors walk natural trails, watch birds and wildlife, and sometimes travel between coastal areas by boat.

Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Corcovado on the **main itinerary**. The journeys differ substantially: you can devote nearly all of a short trip to the country's south or include the park in a much longer journey encompassing volcanoes, cloud forests and the Caribbean coast.

Three questions matter when choosing: **how many days are devoted to Corcovado itself, how access to the forest trails is organised, and what fills the remaining days**. A park appearing in a tour title does not establish the length of the hike.

## Short five-day journeys: rainforest, Sirena Station and the ocean

On [“Costa Rica: Real Gems”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/), the nature-focused portion begins on **day 2**. Following a flight from San José to Palmar Sur, travellers continue by boat along the [Sierpe River](/costa-rica/place/sierpe/). The group stays at Rancho Corcovado lodge. On **day 3**, they visit **Sirena** ranger station and walk forest trails with a naturalist guide. Day 4 includes scuba diving near [Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/). The included services cover an English-speaking guide, domestic flights, transfers and meals on the specified days.

[“Real Treasures of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-san-jose-treasures/) also lasts **five days**, but the details differ. On day 2, travellers reach the southern coast via Sierpe and on day 3 hike Corcovado's trails. Accommodation is planned at Casa Corcovado. Day 4 features a sea outing to Caño with **snorkelling**, not an obligatory scuba dive. This tour includes a **Russian-speaking guide**.

| Tour | Main consideration |
|---|---|
| [Real Gems](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) | Sirena and scuba diving at Caño |
| [Real Treasures](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-san-jose-treasures/) | Corcovado hiking and snorkelling |

Both journeys suit travellers who want to spend several days specifically near rainforest and ocean, rather than most of their time transferring between distant regions. Differences in guiding language and underwater activities matter more than the similar tour names.

## Corcovado on a longer 14-day tour

[“The Best of Costa Rica”](/costa-rica/tour/best-of-costa-rica/) is a **14-day** journey. Before reaching the southern coast, the route includes [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), the [Arenal Volcano area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) and [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/).

Participants head for Corcovado on **day 10**: they travel to the Sierpe River, board a boat and reach [Drake Bay](/costa-rica/place/drake-bay/). **Day 11** is dedicated to exploring Corcovado's forest on foot, while **day 12** is a sea excursion to Caño Island with snorkelling. The journey then returns towards San José.

Choose this option for a combination of the country's natural regions. Corcovado occupies several consecutive days, but it is just one part of the trip. If you want to maximise your time on trails in the southern park, a shorter specialist itinerary may offer more focused experiences.

## Reaching Corcovado: Sierpe, Drake Bay and Sirena

A journey to Corcovado involves several places that are easy to confuse. **Sierpe** is one route to the coast, following a river through mangroves. **[Drake Bay](/costa-rica/place/drake-bay/)** is an accommodation area and boat departure point. **Sirena** is a ranger station inside the national park, where forest walks begin.

“Real Gems” specifically describes taking a boat from the Drake area to Sirena, with an approximate **50-minute crossing** in its itinerary. Arrival involves landing on a beach and changing shoes before walking the trails. This is an arrangement specific to that route, not a universal travel time for every park sector.

Costa Rica's protected areas system, SINAC, identifies several official visitor sectors in Corcovado, including **Sirena, San Pedrillo and La Leona**. They differ in access, trails and duration of journeys. SINAC describes marine access to Sirena from the Drake, Sierpe and Puerto Jiménez areas. Choose a tour according to its stated sector rather than assume that every excursion called “Corcovado” follows the same route.

## Wildlife encounters and why sightings cannot be guaranteed

Corcovado is known for its diversity of tropical ecosystems. Colourful birds, monkeys and other mammals can be found along forest trails, while large predators live in more remote parts of the park. Even with an experienced naturalist, however, a jaguar or other rare animal cannot be promised on a particular day.

More accessible observations are rewarding in their own right: bird calls, animal tracks, the structure of tall trees, coastal forest, and vegetation changing along streams and trails. A guide helps you notice details that are easy to miss when walking quickly on your own.

[Wildlife-watching tours in Costa Rica](/interests/wildlife/tours/costa-rica/) let you compare Corcovado with other regions. Tortuguero, for instance, introduces river canals, while Monteverde offers humid montane forest. They provide different observation conditions and are not interchangeable merely because both are in a tropical country.

## Permits, safety and preparing for the walk

Corcovado is a protected area with regulated access. SINAC requires **advance reservations**; routes to Sirena have rules requiring accompaniment by a registered guide. Visitors need documentation so that their entry authorisation can be checked. The precise booking procedure, accessible sector and rules for your travel date are confirmed when arranging the trip.

Stay on designated trails in the park. Do not feed or chase animals, collect plants, litter or swim off park beaches: there can be dangerous currents along the shore. For hiking, bring comfortable closed footwear, water in an approved container and lightweight clothing offering rain and sun protection; keep your belongings protected from spray during boat transfers.

Landing conditions, weather and the state of the ocean affect the day's actual sequence. When comparing itineraries, therefore, consider not only the description of the forest walk but also **where you will sleep the preceding night**. Staying around Drake Bay makes an early departure for Sirena easier than trying to combine that visit with a long transfer from the country's central region in a single day.

## Corcovado or Caño Island: which matters more to you?

These two nearby natural destinations offer different experiences. **[Corcovado](/costa-rica/place/corcovado-national-park/)** means forest trails and land-based wildlife watching. **[Caño Island](/costa-rica/place/cano-island/)** means marine ecosystems and excursions on the water. They follow one another in several Ada Tours programmes but take place on different days.

If hiking in nature is your priority, compare the length of the forest route and the park sector. If marine life interests you, check the format of the Caño day: snorkelling and scuba diving are not equivalent. For journeys across different regions, see the [Costa Rica tours catalogue](/costa-rica/tour/) and compare how much time is spent on the road.

## Frequently asked questions about Corcovado tours

### How many days are needed to experience Corcovado?

In the shorter five-day Ada Tours journeys, one day is devoted to the principal hike, with the neighbouring days spent on travel and Caño Island. The 14-day itinerary also includes a dedicated park day. Choose based on whether you mainly want to explore the southern rainforest or several of Costa Rica's natural regions.

### Can Sirena be visited without booking ahead?

Organised visits to Sirena require advance authorisation under current SINAC rules and a registered guide. The specific procedure is confirmed when arranging the trip, as it depends on the sector.

### Where is Drake Bay in relation to the park?

[Drake Bay](/costa-rica/place/drake-bay/) lies on the Pacific coast of the Osa Peninsula and serves as a departure point for boats to Corcovado. Sirena Station itself is inside the park's protected area.

### Is scuba diving included on every tour through Corcovado?

No. [“Real Gems”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-gems/) includes diving at Caño, whereas [“Real Treasures”](/costa-rica/tour/costa-rica-san-jose-treasures/) offers snorkelling. Check the marine activities in the tour you choose.

### Is it worth choosing the 14-day trip just for Corcovado?

If your main goal is a hike in the southern rainforest, the shorter tours offer a more direct route. The 14-day journey makes sense if you also want to see [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), volcanic regions and cloud forest, with Corcovado as one of several nature-focused stages.

## Doka Coffee Estate: how Costa Rican coffee is made

[Doka Coffee Estate](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/), also known as Hacienda Doka, is in the Sabanilla area of Alajuela province, on coffee-growing slopes near Poás Volcano. It is a working estate where visitors can follow the production process: cultivating coffee plants, picking ripe cherries, processing the beans, drying and roasting.

For travellers, the estate combines agricultural scenery with a tangible craft. After such a visit, a cup of coffee makes more sense: you understand why coffee cherries must be processed first, how production stages differ and why taste depends on more than the roasting level.

## What you see on a Hacienda Doka tour

A coffee tour generally begins with the plants and the conditions in which they grow. You can see coffee shrubs, cherries at different stages of ripeness, and learn why coffee trees need tending long before harvest.

The next stage is separating the coffee cherry's pulp from the bean. Visitors learn about processing, washing and drying, followed by preparing the beans for roasting. Hacienda Doka is also known for its traditional coffee-processing equipment. It offers a comparison with the familiar experience of a modern café, where customers see only the finished drink.

The final part of a visit usually covers roasting and flavour. Check the tasting format, duration and coffees offered for the particular excursion: independent Hacienda Doka tours and a tour operator's itinerary may include different services.

## Why coffee estates are found near Poás

The [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) area includes highland farming districts with a humid climate. Elevation, temperature, rainfall and soil conditions affect the cultivation of coffee plants and the ripening of cherries. But volcanic soil alone cannot determine in advance the flavour of every local coffee variety.

At the estate, ask specific questions: how long the cherries take to ripen, how they are sorted, when harvesting occurs and what changes during processing and roasting. In this way, coffee becomes part of discovering [Costa Rica's](/costa-rica/) agriculture, rather than just a souvenir at the end of an excursion.

## When to visit and what you can see

A coffee estate is interesting throughout the year, but the season affects which production stages are underway during your visit. At one time you may see flowers and developing cherries, and at another ripe fruit, harvesting and processing. Equipment displays and explanations can be available even without ripe cherries, but actual demonstrations depend on the farm's current work.

Alajuela and the foothills of Poás have different weather from the hot coast: temperatures may be lower and rain can start unexpectedly. Bring comfortable walking shoes and light rain protection. Before combining the estate with the volcano, check crater access and the forecast, as conditions at Poás can change independently of the coffee tour schedule.

## Frequently asked questions about Doka

### Where is Hacienda Doka?

In the Sabanilla area of Alajuela province, near [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/). It pairs well with an excursion programme in the country's central region.

### Can a coffee tour be combined with Poás?

Yes. This combination features in [Ada Tours itineraries](/costa-rica/tour/classic-costa-rica-san-jose-monteverde-arenal/). The key is to check the time allowed for each stop and current conditions for visiting the volcano.

### Does the coffee cherry harvest take place all year?

No. Farm work varies by season. Visitors may learn about processing and roasting even when harvesting is not taking place before their eyes.

### Is a tasting included in every tour visiting Doka?

There is no basis for assuming this is included in every programme. Check the exact inclusions of your chosen tour or standalone excursion; the estate's general description does not define which services have been paid for.
